Why this team. What must it pass.

Eight community lineups, investment guidance and executable thresholds. Runs locally without the game.

Recommendations come from KizunoV’s sheet and video, read on 20 October 2026. Levels, upgrade labels and equipment advice describe recommended investment, not a proven minimum. A threshold pass below applies to the supplied model inputs; no team clear is established.

Choose a team to investigate

Source baseline: level 60 and Soulforge 10 unless stated. “Four copies” means fully upgraded Wheel effect. E-level, OE and AA remain distinct source labels; importing a lineup leaves combat stats unknown.

Plan several teams

Select lineups above to check shared characters and Posse. Search lists the largest conflict-free subsets of those selected templates. Equipment, borrow rules, upgrades and wave assignment still need review.

    Damage worksheets: two inputs, every branch

    Use the same grid format as the historical sheets, with separately labeled noncritical, critical and expected pre-hit damage. Each cell calls the recovered engine.

    Ability inputs and complete branch results

    The raw input supports up to eight labeled ability/setup rows with explicit cost notes. Row and column scales must be supplied; this does not infer coefficients for a named character or pay skill costs. Probability is supplied, not reconstructed from a displayed Crit Rate.

    

    Visible Rotan formula audit: the three unobscured screenshot rows are reproduced by weighting only the critical branch. At STR 100, including the noncritical branch gives 22,072.956 instead of 19,950 under the same displayed 74.6% probability. This is an arithmetic correction; the game’s actual skill coefficients, build and discrete critical-roll probability remain unverified. The Vortice RM ledgers also sum to 1,036.8 and 939.6, consistent with the displayed rounded totals, without validating their damage formulas.
    

    

    Optimize a damage threshold
    Compare six explicit Wheel setups and every order of two paid actions. The example isolates why setup before burst and refinement can matter.
    

    Synthetic demonstration: two available one-cost Strikes, 2 Compute, 100/500 resolved base values, neutral target, explicit Arachne pursuit after setup and Doomsday owner attack 1,000. These are demonstration inputs, unrelated to the listed teams’ actual levels or stats. No Keyflare or full battle loop is simulated.

    Use your own explicit simulation inputs
    Replace candidate timelines with complete property maps and supported paid actions. The search checks the full factorial against the evaluation cap. It does not derive stats from E3, OE or AA.
    

    

    Pass a fixed enemy-pressure threshold
    

    Season 71 Zone 3’s recorded hits are held fixed. Supply candidate-specific HP, effective healing at each turn start, and your horizon. The search finds minimum fresh Block per turn and checks that one less fails. It cannot predict a different team’s enemy actions or verify a clear.

    Evidence and remaining gaps
    The companion guides explain resource bottlenecks and matchup choice. Flares’ team-building guide adds a useful checklist: carry, enabling supports, then reliable debuffs and survival. Its tier lists and damage totals are not matched simulation inputs.
    The repo’s recovered Wheel engine checks pursuit ownership, timing and trigger caps. Complete candidate HP, Keyflare/Posse loops, hands, enemy responses and unsupported upgrades are still missing. The inspected engine builds predate these October guides.
